Location: /Users/bob/git/src/github.com/buvis/gems/src/tools/backup/runner.py

Reuse: existing backup records, capability, runner and console conventions.

Contract (verbatim):

- **Description**: One `now` per run feeds every stamp expansion.
- **Inputs**: `now: datetime`.
- **Outputs**: `_expand_stamp(pattern, now)` uses it; when `now` is absent it falls back to `datetime.now()`.
- **Behavior**: `Runner` takes `now = datetime.now()` once per `run`/`plan` call and passes it as a kwarg.

#### Feature: Duplicate output rejection
- **Description**: Two selected instances may not resolve to one output path.
- **Inputs**: plan entries of the selected instances.
- **Outputs**: for each group sharing a resolved `out`, every instance in the group yields `StepResult(name, success=False, message="output '<out>' is also the output of '<other names, comma separated, sorted>'")` and is not executed; the others run.
- **Behavior**: compared as `os.path.normpath` of the expanded path with `~` expanded; applies to `run`, `--dry-run` and `--plan`.



Acceptance criteria:

tasks.name: [D1] src/tools/backup/runner.py
tasks.description:
### Findings (verbatim)
- 🟠 src/tools/backup/runner.py:36: `Runner.run` now calls `_plan`/`capability.plan` before `_run_instance` and outside its `try/except` (src/tools/backup/runner.py:36). Any OSError from the new metadata checks escapes the generator: `out.exists()`, `is_dir`, `is_symlink`, or a RuntimeError from `resolve` on a symlink loop. `_run_plan` in src/tools/backup/cli.py catches only `FatalError`, so the user sees a raw traceback and every other selected instance is skipped. I reproduced it with one instance whose `out` sits under a chmod-000 dir, plus one good instance. At base 7f4b462 that step fails ("bad failed: [Errno 13] …") and the good instance still archives. At HEAD the run dies with PermissionError and no archive is written. `--plan` crashes the same way. No test covers this. Fix: catch per instance in `_plan` and turn the error into a `fail` entry, the same way `_run_instance` handles it. (found by: ALICE, BLAKE, BOB)
- ⚪ src/tools/backup/runner.py:62: `_plan` tests `capability is None` twice (runner.py:51 and :62, the second with `continue`). Move `outputs.setdefault(...)` into the `else` branch and drop the second check. Additional wording: `_plan` computes `os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(entry.out))` twice per entry, and it checks `capability is None` twice. Computing the key once in the first loop removes both repeats. (found by: ALICE, BOB)

### Acceptance criteria
- Every quoted finding no longer reproduces.
- Add regression tests for the quoted behavioral failures before implementing fixes.
- Preserve FatalError propagation, per-instance failure reporting, independent-instance execution, and duplicate-output safety.
- Run the normal work pipeline, required quality gates, and independent per-task review.

tasks.name: [D1] src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py
tasks.description:
### Findings (verbatim)
- 🟡 src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:80: `TarArchive.plan` resolves `engine` without `run`'s `or _ENGINE_PYTHON` fallback. `engine: ""` now plans as `fail "unknown engine ''"`, and `Runner.run` stops on any plan `fail`. So a config that base archived with python-tarfile (reproduced) now fails in run and in `--dry-run`. That breaks the PRD rule "`--dry-run` is unchanged". (found by: ALICE, BLAKE, BOB)
- 🟡 src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:78: `plan` lacks `run`'s "no source configured" / "no out path configured" guard. An empty `source` plans as `run` with source `.` (the cwd) and exits 0, while the real run fails (reproduced). An empty `out` resolves to `.` with `[replaces existing]`, and two empty outs get reported as a duplicate collision. The preview does not match what a run would do. (found by: ALICE, BLAKE, BOB)
- ⚪ src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:161: `_run_validated` re-reads `label` and `engine` from kwargs (tar_archive.py:161-162), though `run` already computed both. Pass them as parameters instead. Additional wording: `_run_validated` parses `label` and `engine` from `kwargs` again, though `run()` already parsed them. `plan()` and `run()` also repeat the same source/out/`cast(now)` setup. This duplication is how the engine `""` drift happened. (found by: ALICE, BOB)

### Acceptance criteria
- Every quoted finding no longer reproduces.
- Add regression tests for the quoted behavioral failures before implementing fixes.
- Preserve FatalError propagation, per-instance failure reporting, independent-instance execution, and duplicate-output safety.
- Run the normal work pipeline, required quality gates, and independent per-task review.

autonomous_decisions.question: How are duplicate outputs represented in Runner.plan and which output spelling appears in collision messages?
autonomous_decisions.assumption: PlanEntry.status is fail; reason is the exact StepResult duplicate message; diagnostics use expanduser+normpath output. Other PlanEntry fields retain capability plan values. This satisfies the PRD both-fail plan scenario.

I reproduced it with one instance whose `out` sits under a chmod-000 dir, plus one good instance. At base 7f4b462 that step fails ("bad failed: [Errno 13] …") and the good instance still archives. At HEAD the run dies with PermissionError and no archive is written. `--plan` crashes the same way. No test covers this. Fix: catch per instance in `_plan` and turn the error into a `fail` entry, the same way `_run_instance` handles it.
autonomous_decisions.reason: bounded supported defect or repeated simplification; queue first-pass regression follow-up

An empty `source` plans as `run` with source `.` (the cwd) and exits 0, while the real run fails (reproduced). An empty `out` resolves to `.` with `[replaces existing]`, and two empty outs get reported as a duplicate collision. The preview does not match what a run would do.

autonomous_decisions.issue: R4: Simplification: `plan` copies `run`'s pre-walk checks one by one: the engine check with the message repeated word for word at tar_archive.py:87 and :136, the source is_dir/exists branch, the containment check, and `_normalize_items`. That copy is how the two drifts above crept in. Move the checks into one shared validator that returns (status, reason) and call it from both `plan` and `run`.

R5: Simplification: `Runner._plan` (runner.py:54-59) and `_run_instance` (runner.py:82-88) build the same `call_kwargs` dict; only `dry_run` differs. Use one `_call_kwargs(name, instance, now)` helper and add `dry_run` at the call site.

Additional wording: `_plan` computes `os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(entry.out))` twice per entry, and it checks `capability is None` twice. Computing the key once in the first loop removes both repeats.

autonomous_decisions.issue: R8: The test builds its expected `reason` by calling `TarArchive().plan(...)`, the code under test, so it can never catch a wrong reason on a `run` row. Assert `""` instead.

R9: The duplicate check compares paths as text only, as the spec says. It misses two names for one file on case-insensitive APFS (`~/Backup/x.tgz` vs `~/backup/x.tgz`) and a relative vs absolute spelling of the same file (`x.tgz` vs `$PWD/x.tgz`). So two instances can still write one archive and race. The docs mention only symlinks as not resolved.
autonomous_decisions.reason: specified lexical normpath behavior; broader file identity is outside PRD scope

autonomous_decisions.issue: R10: `replaces` uses `out.exists()`, which follows symlinks. A dangling symlink at `out` reports `replaces=False` even though `os.replace` will overwrite it. The rest of plan uses `lexists`, so this is inconsistent.
R11: The `_run_plan` docstring still says it only runs and renders steps. It does not mention the `plan_only` branch that prints plan rows and never executes anything.
R12: Unconfirmed whether README.md documents backup CLI flags. The capsule invariant says every CLI change updates README.md, but only backup.rst and CHANGELOG.md were touched.
autonomous_decisions.reason: README lists the tool only; it does not enumerate backup flags; rg inspection refuted missing flag documentation
